Asymmetric Petasis reaction for the synthesis
of chiral a- and b-butadienyl amines †
Yi-Wen Xie, ‡ Zhen-Ni Zhao, ‡ Zi-Wei Lin, ‡ Yu-Hao Wang, Ya-Qun Liu and
Yi-Yong Huang
 *
The Petasis reaction using (1 S,2R)-1-amino-2-indanol as the sub-
strate and an activator to construct a- and b-butadienyl amines in
optically pure forms was realized, which are otherwise diﬃcult to
prepare. The reactions feature a metal-free nature, broad substrate
scope, complete regioselectivities ( c-selectivity of pinacol homo-
allenyl- and isoprenylboronates), and high to excellent chirality
induction (up to 420 : 1 dr). The favored nucleophilic addition
across the Si-face of the imine intermediate was explained using
DFT calculations of the six-membered chair-like transition state.
Petasis reaction1 using three components of carbonyls, amines
and boron-reagents, as the nucleophile-variation of classic
Mannich reaction, has become a versatile tool for the construc-
tion of enantiopure functionalized amine derivatives.
2 Apart
from the diol,3 hydroxy–thiourea4 and transition-metal5 catalysis,
neighbouring hydroxyl group activation through boronate ligand
exchange between a hydroxyl group and a boronate ester or acid
reagent has proved to be a robust and reliable strategy for the
nucleophilic addition to imine intermediates via ac l o s e ds i x -
membered transition structure.
6 This features a metal-free and
easily-handled transformation, as well as a three-component one-
pot synthesis without the requirement of isolating imines in
advance. By employing this tactic, the hydroxyl group at the
a-position of aldehyde or amine components enables the synthesis
of a-functional amines from various boron-containing reagents,
such as aryl,
7 allenyl and alkenyl 8 and allyl reagents. 9 Yet the
application of this synthetic strategy with novel allylboron-type
reagents to address the synthetic difficulty of some important chiral
scaffolds remains rather underexplored, albeit highly in demand.
a-Butadienyl amines (2-aminomethyl-1,3-dienes) are valuable
synthons for diarylmethylamines
10 through Diels–Alder reactions.
They are also important structural units in natural products, such
as dienic a-amino acids found in the leaves of the ornamental
shrub Philadelphus coronaries(Fig. 1).11 Thus far, some synthetic
strategies have been documented to build this type of molecules.
On the contrary to the gradual progress in racemic synthesis,
12 the
corresponding asymmetric version remains rare. In 2005, Botta’s
group reported the synthesis of chiral 2-( N-1-acetyl-1-arylmethyl)-
1,3-butadienes through the microw ave-assisted ethylene–alkyne
cross-metathesis of ethylene and chiral 1-arylpropargyl amides13
(Scheme 1a).14 Hiemstra’s group demonstrated the synthesis of
enantiopure diene amino acids via the addition of allenylmethyl-
silane into N-acyliminium ion, followed by an enzymatic kinetic
resolution (Scheme 1b).15 In this context, the development of a
facile and general asymmetric strategy for the construction of
chiral a-butadienyl amine derivatives remains a challenging, but
rewarding task.
Since the Petasis reaction process is a g-selective substitu-
tion of allylboronates on the basis of the Zimmerman–Traxler
model, no rearrangement in the carbon chain of b-substituted
allylboronates ( e.g. isoprenylboronates) will occur when trans-
forming into the final products; however, the carbon chain of
g-substituted allylboronates ( e.g. homoallenylboronates) will be
changed. As it turns out, the structural modification at various
sites of allylboronates entails important change in the back-
bone of products. Previously, we have applied pinacol homo-
allenyl- and isoprenylboronates into the installation of chiral
1,3-butadienyl
16 and isoprenyl 17 carbinols through a Brønsted
acid activation strategy, respectively. They both feature the
g-regioselectivity of two boronate reagents. We envisage that
these two boronate-reagents could be utilized in the synthesis

of chiral a-butadienyl amines and b-butadienyl amines by virtue
of an asymmetric Petasis reaction (Scheme 1c). As a part of our
continuous efforts in developing novel synthetic methodologies
with boronate reagents,
18 we herein report this study.
To validate the feasibility of the asymmetric Petasis reaction
using aldehyde 1a and pinacol homoallenylboronate 2a for the
synthesis of chiral 2- a-butadienyl amines 4, we commenced our
study on screening various chiral 1,2-aminols 3, since the
hydroxy group is essential for the Petasis reaction. 6 The key
task is to solve the diastereoselective problem. In the presence
of 50.0 mg of a molecular sieve (4 Å MS) in MeOH at room
temperature (r.t.), chiral 1,2-aminols 3a–c were investigated,
delivering chiral a-butadienyl amines 4 in good yields but with
low diastereoselectivities (Table 1, entries 1–3). No reaction
using (1 S,2R)-2-aminocyclohexanol 3d was found (entry 4).
(1S,2R)-1-Amino-2-indanol 3e displayed better performance,
affording the corresponding product in 94% yield with 3 : 1 dr
within 12 h (entry 5). To our surprise, the reaction without any
molecular sieves proceeded much faster, which suggests that a
small amount of H
2O generated in situ from the condensation
of amine and aldehyde is probably beneficial to releasing
product via hydrolysis (4 h vs. 12 h, entries 5 and 6). In order
to improve the diastereoselective result with 3e, different
combinations of a non-protic solvent and 5.0 equiv. of MeOH
were studied (entries 7–11; see Table S1 in the ESI †); to our
delight, the DMSO media enabled an enhanced dr (11.3 : 1) and
a satisfactory yield (95%, entry 11; see Table S1 in ESI †), which
was identified as the optimal reaction conditions. For comparison,
indanamine3f was used under otherwise identical reaction condi-
tions, or at an elevated temperature; however, the reaction did not
proceed at all; this indicates the essential role of a hydroxy group
(entry 12).
Under the optimized reaction conditions, a number of aryl
and aliphatic aldehydes were readily scoped (Scheme 2). Firstly,
the eﬀects of diﬀerent substituents ( R
0) at the phenyl group on
the reactivity and diastereoselectivity were evaluated. The incor-
poration of electron-donating groups (Me– and MeO–) at the
para-position resulted in inferior dr values ( 4b and 4c);
however, the electron-neutral (F–, Cl– and Br–) and electron-
withdrawing (–CO
2Me and –NO 2) groups were more beneficial
to the diastereoselective outcome. In these cases, 90% to 94%
yields and all 420 : 1 dr were observed ( 4d–h). For the meta-
substituted aldehydes, perfect dr values were obtained inde-
pendent of the electronic nature of the substituents; whereas,
the yields of the examples with electron-withdrawing substitu-
ents (–CF
3, –CN and –CO 2Me; 4k–m) were slightly lower than
those of the other two cases ( 4i, j ). A single example of ortho-
substituted phenyl aldehyde was studied to provide product 4n
in 86% yield with 420 : 1 dr. In addition, two disubstituted
aromatic aldehydes were also tolerated in the Petasis reaction
with excellent yields and dr values ( 4o, p ). 2-Naphthylaldehyde
underwent Petasis 1,3-butadienylation smoothly to give pro-
duct 4q in 92% yield with 420 : 1 dr. Finally, three aliphatic
aldehydes were successfully employed in the reaction, affording
products 4r–t in high yields with perfect dr values except
isobutyraldehyde 4s (12 : 1 dr).
b-Butadienyl amine (2-aminoethyl-1,3-diene or isoprenylamine)
19
is the homologue ofa-butadienyl amine, which can be preparedvia
a similar synthetic strategy–Petasis reaction with pinacol isoprenyl-
boronate 2b. Compared with the reaction conditions mentioned
above for Petasis butadienylation, less volume of DMSO (0.2 mL)
was required for the Petasis isoprenylation to promote the complete
consumption of the aldehyde starting material. As depicted in
Scheme 3, a wide range of aromatic aldehydes with varied

substituents and aliphatic aldehydes participated in the Petasis
isoprenylation reaction. Monosubstituted phenyl aldehydes
including electron-rich and electron-poor substituents ( R
0’) at
the ortho-, meta-a n d para-positions were first studied, providing
the corresponding b-butadienyl amines 5b–q in 84–99% yields
with up to 420 : 1 dr. Electron-rich groups (except tBu-group) at
the para-position and substituents at the ortho-position (except
F-atom) were not good for the diastereoselectivity, and dr values
lower than 20 : 1 were obtained. In addition, 3,4-dimethyl and
3,5-dibromo phenyl aldehydes were also applied to furnish
products 5r, s in high yields with perfect dr values. The use of
2-naphthyl and heteroaromatic aldehydes afforded products
5t–w in 80–99% yields with 8.5 : 1 to 420 : 1 dr; the absolute
configuration of the newly formed stereogenic carbon center of
5u was unambiguously assigned to be S based on the results of
X-ray crystallographic analysis.
20 Thus, the absolute configura-
tions of other aryl isoprenylated products were determined
by analogy. Finally, two aliphatic aldehydes were used to produce
b-butadienyl amines 5x and 5y in 82–85% yields with 420 : 1 dr.
In order to understand the observed stereochemical out-
comes, density-functional theory (DFT) calculations of the key
transition state have been carried out by using the Gaussian 09
suite of programs (see the details in the ESI †). As depicted
in Fig. 2, the diﬀerence of calculated free energy barrier
(D(DG
‡)= /C04.44 kcal mol /C01) between transition states TS-Si
and TS-Re for the isoprenylboration reaction indicates that the
process is favorable for addition through the Si-face of the
imine part to generate the desired adduct 5a. Based on the 3D
model of the transition states, the indan moiety in TS-Re

exhibits a much closer distance to the chair-like six-membered cycle
(the nearest neighbor distance of 2.18 Å) than TS-Si, which may
result in increased steric repulsion and a higher free energy barrier.
Toward exhibiting the synthetic utility of the isoprenylamine
5a, Diels–Alder reactions using dimethyl fumarate and diethyl
butynedioate to provide chiral cyclohexenyl ( 6, 88% yield and
1 : 1 dr) and cyclohexadienyl methylamines ( 7, 78% yield and
420 : 1 dr) were accomplished, respectively (Scheme 4). With
compound 7 in hand, the asymmetric synthesis of optically
pure 1,2-diarylethylamine 9 was completed through two steps
of methylation and oxidative aromatization.
In summary, a synthetic approach to chirala-a n db-butadienyl
amine skeletons has been established via asymmetric Petasis
reactions with pinacol homoalle nyl- and isoprenylboronates,
respectively. A wide range of aromatic and aliphatic aldehydes
w e r ea p p l i e dw i t hu pt o9 9 %y i e l da n d420 : 1 dr. (1 S,2R)-1-
amino-2-indanol plays a key role in enabling the transformation
and chirality induction. The DFT calculations of the six-
membered chair-like transition states shed light on the experi-
mentally observed isoprenylboration across the Si-face of the
imine intermediate. The synthetic application of isoprenylamine
for chiral 1,2-diarylethylamine has been demonstrated. Further
endeavours to achieve asymmetric catalysis with various allylbor-
onates are ongoing in our lab.
